## The Principal's Hall and the two offices, composed

3 rows, each painted twice: the three rooms on the staff steps drawn afresh, each as the inside of its own building in the yard you chose.

Run this in the **local ComfyUI**. Press **Run** once.

Each row is one picture, painted twice: **version A** on top, **version B** under it. You choose between them afterwards.

The **Load Image** boxes on the left should already show their pictures. If one shows an error, click **choose file to upload** and pick the file with the same name from `JJK Game images/ui2/early`.

**Cost:** 6 pictures, about **$0.96** (Nano Banana Pro, about $0.16 a picture, charged to your Comfy account).

You don't need to save anything: the results go to ComfyUI's output folder and Claude picks them up from there.

If it stops with a rate-limit or "high demand" error, wait a minute and press **Run** again: a finished picture is reused, not paid for twice (as long as ComfyUI hasn't been restarted).

widgets_values: This is a background picture for a visual novel: a new picture of one room of a traditional Japanese mountain school, built of timber and white plaster. Picture 1 is the yard this room's building stands on, already painted: the same school. Picture 2 is this room's own building, cut from picture 1 and seen from outside: the new picture is the inside of that building, and its front wall is the same wall seen from inside. Do not copy the camera or the layout of either picture: the new picture is taken indoors, and it shows the room, not the outside of the building. THE PLACE: the inside of a teacher's office, the small detached house with one very large window that stands on the left of picture 1 and is shown close up in picture 2. It is a bright, comfortable sitting room, about eight metres long and six wide, with pale plaster walls, dark timber posts and a timber ceiling. I stand inside at one end and look along the room. The left wall is the front of the house seen from inside. Near me in it a sliding door stands open: this is the way out, with the paved yard outside. Beyond the door the one very large window fills the rest of that wall from low sill to head, and through it I see the yard's paving and gravel in sunlight, a low stone wall and cedars. Against the far end wall stands a long, deep sofa. In front of it a low table is covered with open boxes of sweets, with paper shopping bags on the floor beside it. Against the right wall, further along than the middle, stands a very large flat television on a low cabinet; the stretch of the right wall nearest me is bare. One paper-shaded lamp hangs from the ceiling, not lit. The floor is polished timber boards, clear and open across the whole bottom of the picture. The picture is seen from a standing person's eye height, the horizon a little above the middle. Leave the right ninth of the picture and the top-left corner free of doors, shelves and anything else a visitor would walk to or use. THE LOOK: a real place you could walk into, drawn as a clean modern anime background. Believable materials (wood grain, glass with soft reflections, stone, plaster, fabric), physically believable light with soft shadows and bounced light, real depth. Clean and well kept: walls are fresh and even, with no stains, cracks, peeling, damp patches or dirt, and there is no dust, litter or fallen leaves on the floor or the ground; everything that belongs to the place is still there. Crisp precise edges, clean clear colour, no film grain, no noise, no canvas texture, no visible brush strokes, no haze or glow washing out detail. Through every window a clear, in-focus view. No people, no animals, no text, no logos. Output a 16:9 picture.

Beyond the door is the round window, through which I see the raked gravel of the yard; beyond that the wall is closed paper screens, glowing with daylight. In the middle of the room, facing me, stands a broad timber desk with neat stacks of paper, a desk lamp and a brush stand on it, and a chair behind it. Behind the desk, the far end wall is shelves of files and boxes. On the right wall, further along than the middle, hangs a large board covered with rows of small pinned paper notices, with no writing that can be read; the stretch of the right wall nearest me is bare. A vase of flowers stands on a low cabinet under the board. The floor is polished timber boards, clear and open across the whole bottom of the picture.
